newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound strengthens in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound strengthens in quiet market.

text.p: The Lebanese pound strengthened against the dollar in the week ended on Friday with trade confined to a tight 15-25 piastres spread at the bottom of the Bank of Lebanon's intervention band, dealers said.
The market was not very active, they said.
The central bank twice adjusted its bid-offer intervention band by 50 piastres during the week to reach 1,550-1,558 Lebanese pounds per dollar from 1,551-1,558 at last Friday's close.

Political events, including a sometimes hard-hitting parliamentary confidence debate on Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's new government followed by a partially effective general strike on Thursday against Hariri's policies, had no impact on the market, dealers said.
"The political events did not affect the market in the least," a dealer with a Beirut bank told Reuters. "The market was very calm."
Most banks ignored Thursday's strike and financial markets including foreign exchange dealers stayed open during the stoppage.
One dealer said the pound traded throughout the week at 1,550.05-1,550.20 per dollar and another said the range was 1,550.0-1,550.25.
"There was good offer of dollars. People were buying Lebanese pounds. It is all because of the expectation of falling interest rates on Lebanese pound treasury bills," the dealer said.
